text: According to the chapter, balanced homodyne detection — the basic CV measurement — has which set of properties?
choices: Requires dilution-refrigerator cooling and detects at most one photon per pulse
Operates at room temperature with quantum efficiency above 99% and gigahertz bandwidth
Measures photon number directly and is the resource that makes a circuit non-Gaussian
Simultaneously measures x and p with no added noise penalty
explanation: The book stresses that homodyne detection runs at room temperature with >99% efficiency and GHz bandwidth using ordinary photodiodes. Choice 0 describes cryogenic single-photon counters (the DV world); choice 2 describes photon-number-resolving detection, not homodyne; choice 3 describes heterodyne, which pays a mandatory one-vacuum-unit penalty per quadrature.
